CHIEF COMPLAINT:
"Police hurt my arm — I think it's broken."

HPI:
29 y/o female brought in by friend after reported interaction with law enforcement approximately one hour prior. Patient states officer "twisted my arm behind my back and slammed me down." C/o severe pain in L wrist, L shoulder, and L cheek. Denies LOC. Denies head strike.

PHYSICAL EXAM:
- L wrist: gross deformity, marked swelling, ecchymosis. Limited ROM secondary to pain. Distal pulses intact, cap refill <2s. Sensation grossly intact.
- L shoulder: tenderness over greater tuberosity. Pain with abduction >30 degrees. Apprehension test positive.
- Face: 3 cm abrasion over L zygoma, no underlying step-off. No septal hematoma.
- No other injuries noted on full skin survey.

IMAGING:
- L wrist XR (3 views): Displaced fracture of distal radius with dorsal angulation. No intra-articular extension. Consistent with FOOSH or torsional mechanism.
- L shoulder XR: No fracture or dislocation visualized. MRI recommended outpatient.

ASSESSMENT:
1. Displaced distal radius fracture, L (S52.501A)
2. Suspected rotator cuff injury, L shoulder (M75.101)
3. Facial abrasion, L (S00.81XA)

PLAN:
Closed reduction performed under conscious sedation. Splint applied. F/u with ortho in 3–5 days. Outpatient MRI L shoulder. Ibuprofen 600 mg PRN, oxycodone #12 for breakthrough pain.
